notes: Continuity audit 2026-10-18 (docs/reviews/continuity-audit-21-40-2026-10-18.md) applied: s006 'Dyna beth ddwedodd Mam' (the socks advice was Elen's in 21); s117 Taid gives the rope used in 37 ('ac ewch â'r rhaff yma'). rhaff is 37's planned word, so here it is a glossed incidental (rhaff: i glymu, i ddringo), not a new lexeme. Taid's handing it over is in his speech only, so no segment is added and IDs stay stable.

Codex review 2026-10-18 applied: B2 'ei chopa hi' (yr Wyddfa feminine; s013 'ei gopa e' kept, antecedent y mynydd); narrator's yr hogan / yr hogyn → y ferch / y bachgen (s080, s085, s087, s098); A5 accepts 'gydag e'; C2 accepts 'Pero a ffeindiodd y bwthyn'; C5 accepts named-subject answers; C8 now asks for the southern equivalents of llefrith and rŵan (northern forms stay receptive); B9 reworded; nodyn_en marks allan as also southern. Verdicts recorded; the lluwch gender / plural question stays open for a fluent human.
Length about 1,590 words against 1,780 (window from 1,602): journey, blizzard, cottage and the giant's news; the narration stays southern (meddai e) while the family's dialogue is northern.

Checker warnings justified: pensa-receptive warnings are the northern prompts of Pensum A 'Dweud yn y De' and the C questions that name llefrith / taid / rŵan only so the learner answers in southern forms; nothing receptive is ever an expected answer. lint-a-ac on 'a ydyn' is the interrogative particle. Local density at the shepherd's first speech (four northern forms, each glossed). Recall of 36's words in 37–40 is up to the next block (37 already recalls bugail, craig, llethr, bwthyn, mam-gu; tad-cu, mawn, lluwch, acen, tafodiaith, rhewi, cynhesu, ci defaid still need a later echo, e.g. Mali's chronicle in 38).

G36 is receptive only. Every northern form the family uses is from the plan's receptive list and course.json dialect_lint allowed_from 36 (gen i / gen ti / gynno fo, rŵan, isio, allan, o / fo, dach chi, dowch, sbïo, hogyn, taid, nain, llefrith, mi + verb) and is glossed '= southern form' at its first use; the southern party keep speaking southern. tad-cu and mam-gu are taught productively here as the southern counterparts (with mas, known since Pennod 7, set against allan). Pensum A is 'Dweud yn y De': every prompt is northern, every answer is a productive southern form; the checker's pensa-receptive warnings on A1–A8 are therefore expected.
Mali's diary is the device for the differences (plan), with a hand-authored SVG text table cy-brenin-01-l36-img-de-gogledd.svg (De ↔ Gogledd, twelve pairs) in the margin.
Recall of 35's words: blino, newid, rhannu (rhannodd), ffôl, doeth, gwendid, arall, gogledd, de, fel, dylai; of 34: gyda'n gilydd, ffug (beard), rhy; of 33: cawr, balch.

Dafi's one deliberate slip is northern 'Mae bol gwag gen i', which contrasts with the chapter's target; Mali gives the southern 'Mae bol gwag gyda fi' at once and he repeats it. Mali half-slips into a northern form herself ('os wyt ti isio… os wyt ti eisiau') and corrects it at once; this is a joke about picking up dialect, not an uncorrected error.

Continuity, matching 37 as written: four days' journey north; a blizzard on the fourth day on the slopes of Eryri; Myrddin's umbrella (15, 20) blows inside out; Cai falls into a drift; Pero hears a sheepdog and leads them to a stone shepherd's cottage. Family: Taid (the old shepherd, white beard), Nain, a grandson and a granddaughter, a young black-and-white sheepdog that befriends Pero. Taid: Rhita lives on the summit of Yr Wyddfa, sits on a big rock, comes down in winter and steals sheep, has a cloak of beards, is very proud ('ei wendid o … mae o'n rhy falch'); the storm will pass in the night and there will be mist in the morning (37 opens with mist). The family learns Arthur is the new king (Mali cannot lie). Taid gives Mali the rope used in 37 ('ewch â'r rhaff yma'; rhaff glossed as an incidental).

Recall pass 2026-10-18: recurrences for Penodau 31–35 vocabulary in the storm, the cottage and the diary (siâp, awgrymu, ofnus, penderfynu, arwain, blaen, rhes, clyfar, gobaith, ysbryd, croesawu, ystafell, gwahodd, gwin, twp, doniol, darn, seremoni, coroni, anrhydedd, coginio, cloch, tywysog, gorffen, nodwydd, edau, siswrn, gludo, ffug, trafod, casglu, gelyn, bygwth, cryfder, rhybudd, erbyn, rhybuddio, heddwch, seren). New segments s301–s315.

cover.alt: In a blizzard on a steep Eryri slope, the travellers struggle towards a small stone cottage with a lit window; a black-and-white sheepdog barks at the door and Pero leads the way.
cover.art_brief: A steep snowy mountainside in Eryri at dusk in a blizzard (mist greys, white, slate; a warm yellow window the only warm light; costume colours muted by dusk and snow). A small low stone cottage with a turf-and-stone roof and a curl of peat smoke sits against the slope among big grey rocks and deep snowdrifts (s035). In the doorway a young black-and-white sheepdog barks (s036). Struggling up through the snow towards it in a line, Pero leading (s304): Pero (large shaggy black-and-white hound, grey muzzle) in front, nose down; Arthur (12, untidy brown hair with a cowlick, freckles; plain blue cloak over a long blue robe with a small red dragon on the chest, hood up over his crown); Cai (15, tall, red-blond, rust-red tunic, red cloak, sword at his belt), a sack on his back with the black-and-white wool beard sticking out of it (s098); Mali (12, long dark braid, dark-blue dress, grey winter cloak) clutching her food sack, a small red head peeping out of it (Dafi, cup-sized red dragon, s007); last, Myrddin (very old, thin, long white beard, round wire spectacles, patched deep-blue robe, tall black brimmed hat) holding a black umbrella blown inside out (s021). No text.

segments.text: Am dri diwrnod, teithiodd y ffrindiau i'r gogledd. Roedd y ffordd yn hir, ac roedd y mynyddoedd yn fwy bob dydd.
Ar y diwrnod cyntaf, roedd y caeau'n wyrdd ac yn wlyb.
Ar yr ail ddiwrnod, roedd eira ar y bryniau.
Ar y trydydd diwrnod, roedd eira ar bopeth, ac roedd y llwybr yn mynd i fyny rhwng creigiau mawr, llwyd.
"Mae fy nhraed i'n rhewi!" meddai Cai. "Dw i ddim yn gallu teimlo fy nhraed i!"

inference_aids.alt: The blizzard on the mountain path: Myrddin's black umbrella blows inside out and lifts him on his toes, Cai has fallen into a snowdrift up to his chin, and Arthur pulls him out.
inference_aids.art_brief: A narrow mountain path among big grey rocks in Eryri in a howling blizzard (mist greys and white). Myrddin (very old, thin, long white beard, round wire spectacles, patched deep-blue robe, tall black brimmed hat) clings to a black umbrella that has blown inside out and is lifting him onto his toes, hat jammed on his head. Cai (15, tall, red-blond, rust-red tunic, red cloak, sword at his belt) has fallen into a deep snowdrift and only his red-blond head and one arm stick out; Arthur (12, untidy brown hair with a cowlick, freckles; plain blue cloak over a long blue robe with a small red dragon on the chest) (blue cloak, hood up) hauls him by the hand. Mali (12, long dark braid, dark-blue dress, satchel) shields her food sack; Pero (large shaggy black-and-white hound, grey muzzle) stands with ears pricked, listening to a distant bark. No text.

inference_aids.art_brief: Inside a small one-room stone shepherd's cottage at night, a low peat fire glowing in the middle of the earth floor, smoke curling up to the roof (warm firelight against grey stone; sheepskins, a crook by the wall). Nain (an old woman, small and lively, dark shawl, white cap) pours warm milk from a jug into a wooden cup held by Cai (15, tall, red-blond, rust-red tunic, red cloak), who has gone very red (s050-s051). The shepherd's grandchildren (a boy of about nine and a girl of about ten, in patched wool, barefoot by the fire) sit on the floor laughing and pointing at Cai (s052). Taid the shepherd (an old man with a white beard, big strong hands, a sheepskin over a grey wool tunic) sits on a stool by the fire. Arthur (12, untidy brown hair with a cowlick, freckles; plain blue cloak over a long blue robe with a small red dragon on the chest, hood still up, the crown completely hidden until s062) and Mali (12, long dark braid, dark-blue dress, grey winter cloak) sit on a bench; Pero (large shaggy black-and-white hound, grey muzzle) lies nose to nose with a young black-and-white sheepdog. No text.

"Barf?" meddai e. "Pam mae gynno fo farf yn ei sach?"
segments.speaker: char-hogyn

segments.text: "Os bydd angen brenin barfog," meddai Cai, "fi fydd y brenin barfog! A dw i'n gallu ei gludo hi gyda mêl!"
segments.speaker: char-cai

segments.text: Edrychodd Taid ar y farf wlân, ac wedyn rhoddodd e ei law ar ei farf e: barf go iawn, dim barf ffug.
"Mae Rhita wedi gweld llawer o farfau," meddai e. "Mae o'n gwybod beth yw barf go iawn."
segments.speaker: char-bugail

segments.text: Roedd Arthur a Myrddin yn eistedd wrth y tân gyda Taid.
"Dyn ni'n mynd i'r Wyddfa," meddai Arthur. "Dyn ni'n chwilio am Rhita Gawr."
segments.speaker: char-arth

segments.text: Roedd Taid yn dawel am amser hir.
"Rhita Gawr," meddai e yn dawel.
segments.speaker: char-bugail

segments.text: "Mae o'n byw ar y copa, ar ben yr Wyddfa, yn y cymylau.
Mae o'n dod i lawr yn y gaeaf, ac mae o'n dwyn ein defaid ni. Mae o'n bygwth pawb."
"Mae gynno fo glogyn o farfau.

inference_aids.gloss: mae gynno fo = mae … gyda fe

segments.text: Mae o'n eistedd ar graig fawr ar y copa, ac mae o'n falch iawn o'r clogyn.
Mae o'n gryf, ond ei wendid o yw hynny: mae o'n rhy falch.
Dach chi'n ddewr, neu dach chi'n ffôl?"
"Dyn ni'n mynd gyda'n gilydd," meddai Arthur. "Dyna ein cryfder ni. Dw i ddim yn gwybod a ydyn ni'n ddoeth. Ond dyn ni ddim yn ffôl."
segments.speaker: char-arth

segments.text: Edrychodd Taid ar y brenin bach, ac wedyn ar Myrddin.
"Dyma fy rhybudd i," meddai e. "Bydd y storm yn mynd yn y nos."
segments.speaker: char-bugail

segments.text: "Erbyn y bore, bydd niwl ar y mynydd.
Ewch yn gynnar, ewch yn araf, ac ewch â'r rhaff yma.
Mae'r llwybr i'r copa'n serth iawn, ac mae'r lluwchfeydd yn ddwfn.
Rhaid dringo am oriau."
"Diolch am ein rhybuddio ni," meddai Myrddin. "Mae dy dân di'n gynnes, ac mae dy deulu di'n dda iawn i ni."
segments.speaker: char-myrddin

segments.text: Yn y nos, roedd y gwynt yn curo ar y drws, ond roedd y bwthyn yn gynnes.
Roedd Dafi'n cysgu yn y sach, ac roedd Cai'n cysgu gyda barf wlân Modlen dan ei ben e.
Ond doedd Arthur ddim yn cysgu. Roedd e'n meddwl am y copa, ac am y cawr balch yn y cymylau.
Drwy'r ffenest fach, roedd e'n gweld y sêr: roedd y storm wedi mynd.
